note.question: How can a city allocate scarce licenses or similar homogeneous quotas while preserving truthful participation and guaranteeing a chosen level of equality with little efficiency loss?
note.overview: Privately informed demanders can strategically misreport values for scarce homogeneous goods. The paper designs an allocation-payment mechanism, proves dominant-strategy truthfulness and ex post individual rationality, and optimizes welfare subject to an equality constraint.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: The planner first selects the two-group mechanism parameters. The n_1 highest bidders enter Group I and receive goods by a paid lottery with probability t_1; remaining players enter Group II and receive the remaining goods by a free lottery with probability t_2. Payments and allocations are implemented, and the planner evaluates efficiency and equality. High reported values compete in a paid lottery and lower reports share a free lottery.

components.label: Solution or estimation method
components.explanation: The authors parameterize all two-group paid/free lottery mechanisms, construct a generalized critical payment, prove truthfulness and individual rationality, and optimize allocation probabilities under an equality constraint. Structural value-shape conditions yield exact or near exact ATL optimality, and worst-case analysis plus simulations quantify performance outside those conditions.
